name: MindGrab Skull Stripping
task: Skull stripping (brain extraction) in any imaging modality
description: A dilated 3D CNN (MeshNet-style) that removes non-brain tissue from a 3D medical image, ported from the mindgrab model in the brainchopC project so it runs as a standard MONAI bundle. The bundle reproduces brainchopC's full inference pipeline: intensity-clip and reslice the input onto a 256x256x256, 1mm, LIA-oriented conform grid, quantile-normalize it, run the network, keep only the largest connected foreground component, reslice the prediction back onto the input's native grid, and floor non-brain voxels of the original image to the image's own minimum intensity.
authors: Fani, Doan, Le, Fedorov, Hoffmann, Rorden, Plis (original MindGrab model); ported to MONAI bundle format by the MONAI Model Zoo community
data_source: Not documented by this port; see the upstream brainchopC project for the original mindgrab training details.
image_classes: single channel data, any modality, any input size/orientation (internally resampled to a 256x256x256, 1mm conform grid)
label_classes: not applicable: output is a skull-stripped copy of the input image, not a label map
pred_classes: 2 channels, channel 0 is background, channel 1 is brain (conform-space network logits, before this bundle's postprocessing reslices and applies the mask)
intended_use: This is an example, not to be used for diagnostic purposes
references: Fani, A., Doan, M., Le, I., Fedorov, A., Hoffmann, M., Rorden, C., Plis, S. 'MindGrab: A spectrally-motivated architecture for accessible deep learning in neuroimaging.' NeuroImage 338 (2026): 122074. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2026.122074
brainchopC, the C reference implementation this bundle ports (private repository)
